messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT detected: tokenization/preproc tail latency spike. p95=1.2s (baseline 200ms), p99=5.6s (baseline 800ms). Streaming stalls observed for some long-response requests. Auto-severity: SEV3 (possible customer impact).
Maya (oncall): I'm paged, looking. Which route/components are lighting up?
Tim (SRE): Preproc queue depth on preproc-worker* climbed to 420. Backpressure to upstream streamers visible. Logs show repeated `TokenizerTimeout` + `TemplateRender` spikes.
Zoe (Eng-ML): Seeing lots of requests hitting JSON mode rendering for tool schemas. Biggest CPU times from `render_tool_schema()` in prompt pipeline.
Raj (eng): Confirmed. Telemetry: 86% of p99 requests had >1 extra eval in prompt template expansion. Correlating with requests that include large tool schemas + JSON mode.
Maya (oncall): Customer impact? Any errors or just latency?
Lena (CS): Some customers reported slow responses in chat sessions, 7 SEV tickets opened; two enterprise customers reporting failed streaming sessions.
Sam (product): Are there safe mitigations we can do without rollback? Can we throttle template expansion or switch modes?
Zoe (Eng-ML): Short-term options: 1) disable JSON mode for streaming routes (can toggle per-route), 2) enable template-cache warm for recent templates, 3) reduce preproc concurrency to avoid head-of-line stalls (helps tail).
Tim (SRE): I'm going to open a canary kill switch for JSON-mode on the streaming route. Command: `rctl set-route-config streaming-prod --json_mode=false --target=canary`
deploy-bot: deploy started: route-config update streaming-prod -> canary users (10%).
Maya (oncall): Rolling canary now. Observability: please watch p95/p99 and streaming stall counts.
Raj (eng): Also noticed a tokenizer GC thrash on nodes running quantized bpe library. I'll restart preproc pods one by one to force warm caches with patched fallback. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/preproc -n inference --grace-period=30`
Zoe (Eng-ML): Quick patch: add short-circuit for tool schemas > 8KB to use schema-summary instead of full JSON in prompt construction. I'll stage patch to preproc-canary.
Tim (SRE): Canary looks promising. After toggling JSON_mode=false for 10%: streaming p95 down from 1.2s -> 320ms within 90s for canary cohort. p99 also dropping but still above baseline.
Lena (CS): Noted improvement for the two reported customers in canary set, they confirm faster streaming.
Sam (product): What's the rollback plan if canary fails?
Maya (oncall): If canary regresses, we'll rollback route-config and re-enable prior behavior. But if it holds, we can expand to 50% in 10min, then 100%. Also plan to patch template rendering to cache summaries ASAP.
Raj (eng): Preproc pod restarts applied to 3/8 pods. Early results: tokenization CPU drops ~22% on restarted pods.
Zoe (Eng-ML): Deployed schema-summary short-circuit to preproc-canary. It reduces render time for big-tool requests from ~350ms -> 45ms.
deploy-bot: preproc-canary deployment succeeded.
Tim (SRE): Metrics after 7min: overall streaming p95=260ms, p99=890ms (still high); stalls count down 78% from peak. Queue depth stabilizing at ~45.
Maya (oncall): Good. Customer impact summary so far: ~12 customers affected intermittently, 2 enterprise ticket escalations, no data loss. Stages: mitigation ongoing, workaround applied.
Lena (CS): I'll send a templated message to affected customers: outage acknowledged, mitigation in progress. CC'ing Sam.
Sam (product): Please note: we should also add a guardrail to the prompt composer in SDKs to avoid full-tool JSON in streaming by default. Filing a follow-up ticket.
Zoe (Eng-ML): Root cause hypothesis: large tool schemas + JSON-mode caused heavy prompt-template rendering and memory churn in preproc -> tail tokenization stalls; exacerbated by GC behavior on quantized tokenizer runtime. Fixes: short-term toggle + schema-summary + pod restarts. Long-term: prompt composer defaults + caching + tokenizer GC tuning.
Maya (oncall): Next actions: 1) Expand JSON-mode disable to 50% in 10m if p99 < 1.5s; 2) Continue rolling restart preproc; 3) Promote schema-summary patch to prod canary and monitor; 4) Draft RCA and customer impact note.
Tim (SRE): I'll coordinate the rollout and set monitoring alert thresholds back to normal once stable for 30m.
Raj (eng): Opening PR to add template size guard and cache TTL; will link here when ready.
Lena (CS): Customer update drafted and ready to send after 30m stable.
Maya (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated if no regressions. Leaving oncall to Tim for postmortem.
Zoe (Eng-ML): Adding telemetry to track `template_render_time` per-request and `tool_schema_size` to help future detection.
Maya (oncall): Thanks team — ongoing notes in runbook: https://redwood.app/runbooks/preproc-tail-latency (internal). Closing thread when p99 < 1s for 30m. :white_check_mark:
